sandhi.note: -aḥ before a: o, with the following a elided (avagraha). Inside the compound, तद् + अङ्गुल्यः keeps its voiced d before the vowel (झलां जशोऽन्ते, 8.2.39).

samasa.sense: the toes; तद् here points back to पादौ, and must be a compound member, since a separate तत् could not agree with the feminine plural अङ्गुल्यः

samasa.literal: by the radiance of the Sun
samasa.sense: from the Sun’s share of the tejas
the fingers, set against the toes (तदङ्गुल्यः) in the line above

morph.note: Nominative plural of the feminine i-stem अङ्गुलि: i becomes y before the ending -अः (अङ्गुल्-यः). The same form ends कराङ्गुल्यः.
Genitive plural of the u-stem वसु, with the long ū and n of the ending -नाम्: the Vasus as a group gave the fingers.

mantras.anvaya: ब्रह्मणः तेजसा पादौ (अभवताम्), अर्कतेजसा तदङ्गुल्यः (अभवन्), वसूनां च (तेजसा) कराङ्गुल्यः, कौबेरेण च (तेजसा) नासिका (अभवत्)।
mantras.anvaya_en: Four nominal clauses with the verb supplied from 2.14–15 (अभवत् / अभवन्); the source is always in the instrumental.
mantras.lit: By the radiance of Brahmā the feet, their toes by the radiance of the Sun; and by the Vasus’ the fingers, and by Kubera’s the nose.
mantras.tr: From Brahmā’s radiance came her feet, from the Sun’s her toes, from the Vasus’ her fingers, and from Kubera’s her nose.
mantras.tr_note: ‘Came’ is supplied; the verse has no verb of its own.

comm.t: The list continues. Brahmā, the creator, gives the feet; the Sun the toes; the Vasus the fingers; Kubera, lord of wealth, the nose. The verse has no verb: the pattern of 2.14–15 carries it.

Brahmā, who led the gods to Śiva and Viṣṇu (2.4), gives the Goddess her feet. The tradition makes much of the Goddess’s feet as the place of refuge and worship, and here the creator’s own tejas forms them.

samasa.literal: by the radiance of the Purifier
samasa.sense: from Agni’s share of the tejas

morph.note: Perfect of √जन्, ātmanepada (ज-ज्ञ्-ए, with loss of the root vowel): ‘was born’. The singular agrees with the collective नयनत्रितयम्.
Past participle of सम् + √भू used as a finite verb: ‘(were) produced’.
Taddhita of relation from प्रजापति, ‘belonging to Prajāpati’. See Uncertain.

mantras.anvaya: तस्याः तु दन्ताः प्राजापत्येन तेजसा सम्भूताः। तथा पावकतेजसा नयनत्रितयं जज्ञे।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two clauses, each with a subject, a verb (participle; perfect) and the source in the instrumental.
mantras.lit: Her teeth came into being by the radiance of Prajāpati; likewise the triad of eyes was born by the radiance of Fire.
mantras.tr: Her teeth were formed from the radiance of Prajāpati, and her three eyes, likewise, from the radiance of Fire.

comm.t: The teeth come from Prajāpati’s tejas and the three eyes from Agni’s. The Goddess has three eyes, like Śiva.
Three eyes are a mark the Goddess shares with Śiva, whose third eye is traditionally the eye of fire. Here all three of her eyes are formed from Agni’s tejas.

flags.uncertain: प्राजापत्येन तेजसा: which Prajāpati is meant is not stated. Since Brahmā’s tejas has already given the feet (2.16), the Prajāpati here is probably another (one of the lords of creatures, such as Dakṣa) or the Prajāpatis as a class; it is translated simply as ‘Prajāpati’. The reading itself is not in doubt.

sandhi.note: Visarga before t becomes s; likewise सम्भवस्तेजसाम्.
Final au before a vowel becomes āv. Here the v is kept (the optional loss of y/v, 8.3.19, applies to the ay/av from e/o, not to āv).
Final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra.

morph.note: Nominative dual of the feminine root-noun भ्रू ‘brow’: before vowel endings ū becomes uv (भ्रुव्-औ).
The construction changes in this verse: instead of an instrumental of source (तेजसा) the radiance stands in the nominative as a predicate, ‘the brows (were) the twilights’ radiance’.

Action noun from सम् + √भू, ‘coming together, origin’. Predicated of शिवा: ‘Śivā was the issue of the radiances’. The masculine noun and the feminine subject do not need to agree: they are subject and predicate.

mantras.anvaya: भ्रुवौ च संध्ययोः तेजः, श्रवणौ च अनिलस्य (तेजः)। अन्येषां च एव देवानां तेजसां सम्भवः शिवा (अभूत्)।
mantras.anvaya_en: Two nominal sentences of the form ‘X (was) Y’s radiance’, then a summary sentence with शिवा as subject and सम्भवः as predicate.
mantras.lit: And the brows (were) the radiance of the two Twilights, and the ears (that) of the Wind; and Śivā was the issue of the radiances of the other gods as well.
mantras.tr: Her brows were the radiance of the two Twilights, her ears that of the Wind; and so the auspicious Goddess arose from the radiance of all the other gods as well.
mantras.tr_note: tr renders सम्भवः … शिवा as ‘the auspicious Goddess arose from’.

comm.t: The description ends with a summary: the rest of the gods contributed too, and the being who arose from all their radiance is called Śivā, ‘the auspicious’. The two Twilights (संध्ये, dawn and dusk) are counted among the givers.

Śivā is the feminine of śiva, ‘auspicious, benign’, and a name of the Goddess as Śiva’s consort. This is the first time the text uses it: the being formed from anger-born radiance is named ‘the auspicious one’.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) has the same name, शिवा (name 53), and श्रीशिवा (name 998). The name is common to many Śākta texts; the two works are distinct.

sandhi.note: The s of तेजस् becomes रु and then u before the voiced r; a + u → o.
After u the visarga is sounded r before the vowel a. -āḥ before the voiced m loses its visarga (via y, which is dropped before a consonant).

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi containing a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (तेजोराशि: तेजसां राशिः)
samasa.literal: she whose origin is the heap of radiance
samasa.sense: born of the gods’ gathered tejas
samasa.alt: Also possible as a pañcamī tatpuruṣa with an adjectival समुद्भवा ‘arisen from the mass of radiance’; the bahuvrīhi is the regular way such a compound qualifies a feminine.

samasa.sense: the gods whom Mahiṣa had oppressed

morph.note: Perfect of प्र + √आप्: the reduplicating a merges with the root’s ā, so the perfect stem is आप्- (3rd pl. आपुः, with the prefix प्रापुः), ‘they obtained’. मुदं प्राप् is the idiom ‘to feel joy’.
A genitive outside the compound that qualifies one of its members (तेजोराशि ‘the mass of radiance of all the gods’). Strict grammar frowns on this, but Purāṇic and epic verse uses it freely.
Absolutive of वि + √लोक्, ‘having beheld’; its agent is अमराः, the subject of the main verb.

mantras.anvaya: ततः महिषार्दिताः अमराः समस्तदेवानां तेजोराशिसमुद्भवां तां विलोक्य मुदं प्रापुः।
mantras.anvaya_en: Subject (महिषार्दिताः अमराः), an absolutive phrase with its object (तां … विलोक्य), and the main verb with its object (मुदं प्रापुः).
mantras.lit: Then, having beheld her, who had arisen from the mass of radiance of all the gods, the immortals, oppressed by Mahiṣa, attained joy.
mantras.tr: Then the gods, so long oppressed by Mahiṣa, looked on her who had arisen from the gathered radiance of them all, and they were filled with joy.

comm.t: The gods see the woman formed from their pooled tejas and rejoice. Their joy closes the account of her birth and opens the giving of gifts (2.20–31).
A modern reading: the gods rejoice at something greater than any of them, which is also their own power given back in a new form.
